labels.app.name: WPods
labels.firstRun.title: Welcome to WPods
labels.firstRun.body: Control your AirPods from Windows: battery, noise control, microphone and more.
labels.firstRun.trayDesc: Closing the window keeps WPods running.
labels.firstRun.micDesc: As "Headset ({label}, {name})", so your audio stays in stereo.
labels.firstRun.startupDesc: So battery and the mic are ready when you are.
labels.empty.title: No AirPods yet
labels.empty.body: Pair your AirPods with this PC in Windows Bluetooth settings, then come back here.
labels.adapter.title: WPods can't use this Bluetooth adapter
labels.adapter.body: Your PC's Bluetooth adapter isn't connected over USB, so WPods can't work with it (error {code}). A USB Bluetooth adapter, such as a small USB dongle, works: plug one in and pair your AirPods with it.
labels.restart.title: Restart needed
labels.restart.body: WPods needs a restart to work. Restart your PC now, or later when it suits you.
labels.restart.confirm: Save your work first. Restart now?
labels.legal.firstRunBody: WPods is an independent, open-source project. It isn't made, sponsored, endorsed or supported by Apple. AirPods and the names of their features belong to Apple Inc.; WPods uses them only to say what it works with. WPods comes with no warranty: you use it at your own risk.
labels.legal.adapterBody: WPods' background service takes over your Bluetooth adapter and passes it back to Windows as a virtual adapter through usbip-win2 by Vadym Hrynchyshyn, so all your Bluetooth devices keep working. When you uninstall WPods, or if this keeps failing, the adapter goes back to Windows' own driver.
labels.legal.footer: Not affiliated with Apple. AirPods is a trademark of Apple Inc.
labels.legal.title: Legal
labels.legal.notAppleBody: WPods is an independent project. It isn't made, sponsored, endorsed or supported by Apple Inc.
labels.legal.trademarksBody: Apple, AirPods, AirPods Pro, AirPods Max, iPhone, iPad and Mac are trademarks of Apple Inc., registered in the U.S. and other countries. Feature names such as Noise Cancellation, Transparency, Adaptive, Conversation Awareness, Personalised Volume, Hearing Aid, Standard, Voice Isolation and Wide Spectrum are Apple's names. WPods uses them only to describe which AirPods and features it works with, and claims no rights to them.
labels.legal.ownFeaturesBody: Where WPods runs its own processing under one of Apple's names, like the mic modes, it is WPods' own implementation and not Apple's technology.
labels.legal.thirdPartyBody: The noise-reduction models and libraries WPods ships belong to their authors and are used under their licences. WPods claims no ownership of them.
labels.legal.licenseBody: WPods is free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3. Copyright (C) 2026 fpndev (rimjoeh) <rimjoeh@gmail.com>. The WPods code and interface are the author's work.
labels.legal.warrantyBody: WPods is provided as is, without any warranty, to the extent the law allows. You use it at your own risk. The author isn't liable for any damage or loss.
labels.legal.contactBody: If you hold rights to something in WPods and want it changed or removed, email rimjoeh@gmail.com. Requests are handled promptly.
labels.pair.title: Pair new AirPods
labels.pair.step2Title: Hold the button on the back
labels.pair.step3Desc: WPods finds them on its own after that.
labels.home.hintBuds: Open the case near your PC, or put your AirPods in your ears.
labels.home.hintMax: Take your AirPods Max out of the Smart Case to wake them.
labels.home.hintElsewhere: Connecting here takes them over from the other device.
labels.home.keysHint: Connect once to enable nearby detection.
labels.home.controlsDesc: Noise modes, press speed, tone volume
labels.nc.title: Noise control
labels.nc.oneBudNote: Noise Cancellation needs both AirPods in, or turn on "Noise cancellation with one AirPod".
labels.nc.outOfEarNote: Put an AirPod in your ear to change noise control.
labels.mic.title: Microphone
labels.mic.desc.notActive: Apps can use your AirPods as the microphone "Headset ({label}, {name})".
labels.mic.desc.live: An app is using your AirPods microphone.
labels.mic.desc.problem: The microphone isn't coming through. Try reconnecting your AirPods.
labels.mic.desc.unsupported: {name} can't send the microphone in stereo. Apps can use it in Hands-Free mode, and the sound turns mono while they do.
labels.mic.note: Not Apple's processing: WPods runs public models locally under these names. Pick them in Windows settings > Mic modes.
labels.mic.modesDesc: Which modes show up and the model each one uses
labels.mic.modesGroupDesc: Modes you turn off disappear from the Home page. Keep at least one.
labels.mixer.title: Mixer
labels.mixer.desc: Hear your mic and other devices in your AirPods
labels.mixer.note: Windows audio plays in your AirPods as usual. Devices you tick play on top of it, each at its own volume.
labels.mixer.enabledDesc: Turn off to silence them all at once. Your picks and volumes stay.
labels.hotkeys.title: Hotkeys
labels.hotkeys.desc: Change noise control, mic modes and more from any app
labels.hotkeys.note: Hotkeys work anywhere in Windows, even with WPods in the tray. To switch something on and off with one key, give Turn on and Turn off the same hotkey.
labels.hotkeys.soundsDesc: A short sound confirms each change. For noise control, your AirPods play their own.
labels.hotkeys.nextNoiseDesc: Same modes and order as press and hold
labels.hotkeys.nextMicDesc: Goes through the mic modes you turned on
labels.hotkeys.againFoot: Press a mode's hotkey again to go back to the mode you had before.
labels.hotkeys.recordHint: Press the keys you want. Esc cancels, Backspace removes the hotkey.
labels.hotkeys.needModifier: Add Ctrl, Alt or the Windows key, so the hotkey doesn't get in the way of typing.
labels.hotkeys.toggle: Switches on and off with one key.
labels.hotkeys.conflict: Also set for {action}. Neither runs until you change one of them.
labels.hotkeys.taken: Windows or another app already uses this hotkey. Pick another one.
labels.hotkeys.reserved: WPods already uses this hotkey to focus the nearby popup. Pick another one.
labels.osd.offNotAllowed: Turn on Allow "Off" in listening modes first.
labels.osd.micModeOff: Turn on {mode} in Mic modes first.
labels.osd.oneMicMode: Only one mic mode is on. Turn on more in Mic modes.
labels.osd.conflict: This hotkey is set for two things that clash. Change it in WPods.
labels.mic.rawDesc: No model, no processing: the mic exactly as it comes in.
labels.features.title: Features
labels.features.earDesc: Pauses audio when you take an AirPod out.
labels.features.earDescMax: Pauses audio when you take them off.
labels.features.conversationDesc: Lowers media and brings voices forward when you speak.
labels.features.duckDesc: How low media goes while you're talking.
labels.features.oneBudDesc: Keeps Noise Cancellation on with a single AirPod in.
labels.features.personalizedVolumeDesc: Adjusts media volume to your surroundings.
labels.features.allowOffDesc: Adds Off to the modes you cycle through by pressing the stem.
labels.features.allowOffDescMax: Adds Off to the modes you cycle through with the noise control button.
labels.features.heartRateDesc: Reads your pulse from the sensors in your AirPods.
labels.features.hearingAidDesc: Uses the hearing settings from your iPhone or iPad.
labels.hearing.title: Hearing Assistance
labels.hearing.setup: Hearing Aid and Media Assist stay off until you set up hearing on your iPhone or iPad.
labels.hearing.bothOn: Hearing Aid and Media Assist on
labels.hearing.callsDesc: Only for calls that use Hands-Free mode.
labels.hr.note: AirPods aren't a medical device. Don't use these readings to diagnose or treat any condition.
labels.controls.title: Controls
labels.stem.title: Press and hold cycles through
labels.controls.pressSpeedDesc: How quickly you need to press twice.
labels.controls.holdDurationDesc: How long to hold before noise control changes.
labels.controls.toneDesc: The chimes your AirPods play, like the connect sound.
labels.windows.title: Windows settings
labels.windows.handsFreeDesc: Keeps audio in stereo. The microphone comes through WPods.
labels.windows.handsFreeNoStereoMic: These AirPods can't send the microphone in stereo. With Hands-Free mode off, they have no microphone.
labels.windows.hdVoiceDesc: Clearer mic, with mic modes. Sound turns mono while the mic is on.
labels.windows.latencyNote: The sound stream stays on, so your AirPods may use more battery.
labels.windows.latencyMicDesc: Your mic is live the moment an app opens it.
labels.windows.latencyMicNote: The mic stays on, so your AirPods may use more battery.
labels.windows.latencyMicHdNote: With HD voice, this keeps the voice link up, so sound stays mono the whole time.
labels.windows.startupDesc: Opens in the tray when you sign in.
labels.windows.themeDesc: Auto follows your Windows app mode.
labels.windows.accentDesc: Matches the colour you chose in Personalisation.
labels.update.title: Updates
labels.update.ready: WPods {version} is ready and installs the next time WPods starts.
labels.update.nowDesc: Updating now pauses Bluetooth for a few seconds.
labels.update.autoDesc: Downloads new versions in the background and installs them the next time WPods starts.
labels.lang.title: Language
labels.lang.foot: Arabic, Hebrew and Urdu lay the window out right to left.
labels.toast.noResponse: Your AirPods didn't respond. Try reconnecting.
labels.toast.connectFailed: Couldn't connect. Make sure the case is open and nearby.
labels.toast.micFailed: Something went wrong with the microphone (error {code}). Try reconnecting your AirPods.
labels.toast.lowLatencyFailed: Low audio latency couldn't start. Make sure your AirPods are the output device.
labels.toast.handsFreeFailed: Couldn't change Hands-Free mode. Try again.
labels.toast.micModelFailed: This model couldn't load (error {code}). WPods keeps using the previous one.
labels.toast.micModeStopped: A microphone mode stopped working and was turned off (error {code}). Reconnect your AirPods to try again.
labels.toast.settingsReset: Your settings couldn't be read, so WPods started with default settings (error {code}).
labels.toast.webviewFailed: WPods couldn't open its window. Make sure Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime is installed (error {code}).
labels.toast.serviceDown: WPods' background service isn't running, so AirPods features are paused (error {code}). Restart your PC, or reinstall WPods if this keeps happening.
labels.toast.restartToFinish: Restart Windows to finish setting up WPods. AirPods features start after the restart.
labels.toast.bluetoothNative: WPods handed Bluetooth back to Windows after repeated problems, so AirPods features are paused (error {code}).
labels.toast.updateFailed: The update couldn't be installed (error {code}). Try again later.
labels.popup.multiSubTwo: Two of your AirPods are nearby.
labels.popup.multiSubThree: Three of your AirPods are nearby.
labels.popup.failedBody: Make sure your AirPods are close to your PC and try again.
